domain: Endocrine, Bone, Nutrition and Toxic Elements

cohorts.name: Primary Hypothyroid Pattern
cohorts.description: Raised TSH with a low or low-normal free T4 - the pituitary driving a failing thyroid gland.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: Thyroid autoantibodies sit in both Thyroid Profile and Autoimmune Disorders in the clinical reference. Lipid parameters are admitted as supporting signals because untreated hypothyroidism raises LDL and is a reversible cause of dyslipidaemia.

supporting.label: LDL raised - a recognised consequence of untreated hypothyroidism

evidence.citation: Jonklaas J et al., ATA Guidelines for the Treatment of Hypothyroidism, Thyroid 2014;24:1670-1751
evidence.note: TSH with free T4 as the primary diagnostic pair; TSH >10 mIU/L marks overt disease.

evidence.citation: Chaker L et al., Lancet 2017;390:1550-62
evidence.note: Subclinical versus overt hypothyroidism and the role of TPO antibodies in predicting progression.

diseases.name: Hypothyroidism
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'High TSH with Low FT3/FT4; TSH + Anti-Thyroglobulin Abs both abnormal (suggests autoimmune origin)'; Related Markers/Tests: TSH, Free T4, Free T3, Anti-Thyroglobulin Antibodies

diseases.name: Autoimmune thyroiditis (Hashimoto's)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'TSH + Anti-Thyroglobulin Abs both abnormal'; Related Markers/Tests: TSH, Free T4, Anti-Thyroglobulin Antibodies, Anti-TPO Antibodies

diseases.name: Atherogenic Dyslipidemia
diseases.dm_basis: Cross-linked as a reversible secondary cause; the Disease Master Cardiovascular row treats lipid abnormality as the risk signal, and hypothyroidism must be excluded before attributing it to primary dyslipidaemia

cohorts.name: Hyperthyroid Pattern
cohorts.description: Suppressed TSH with raised free T3 or free T4 - excess circulating thyroid hormone.

supporting.label: ALP raised - accelerated bone turnover in thyrotoxicosis

evidence.citation: Ross DS et al., ATA Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hyperthyroidism, Thyroid 2016;26:1343-1421
evidence.note: Suppressed TSH with raised free hormones as the biochemical definition; aetiology requires further testing.

diseases.name: Hyperthyroidism
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low/suppressed TSH with High FT3/FT4'; Related Markers/Tests: TSH, Free T4, Free T3; Severity/Urgency: 'urgent if thyroid storm suspected'

cohorts.name: Hyperandrogenic / Insulin-Resistant Ovarian Pattern
cohorts.description: Androgen excess with a raised LH/FSH ratio and metabolic features - the biochemical picture that supports polycystic ovary syndrome in a female patient.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The clinical reference PCOS row itself lists Insulin (Fasting) and Fasting Blood Glucose alongside the hormone markers, so Diabetes Monitoring parameters contribute directly to this Hormones-profile cohort.

triggers.label: Total testosterone above the female reference range
Free testosterone above the female reference range

supporting.label: SHBG low - raises free androgen availability
AMH raised - reflects increased antral follicle count
Fasting glucose in the impaired range
Prolactin normal - argues against hyperprolactinaemia as the cause of cycle disturbance

evidence.citation: Teede HJ et al., International Evidence-Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of PCOS, 2023
evidence.note: Rotterdam criteria; biochemical hyperandrogenism plus ovulatory dysfunction, with insulin resistance as a common metabolic feature. AMH may substitute for follicle count in adults.

evidence.citation: Rotterdam ESHRE/ASRM-Sponsored PCOS Consensus Workshop Group, Fertil Steril 2004;81:19-25
evidence.note: Original consensus definition requiring two of three criteria.

diseases.name: PCOS
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated androgens with irregular cycles and insulin resistance markers'; Related Markers/Tests: Testosterone, LH, FSH, Insulin (Fasting), Fasting Blood Glucose

diseases.name: Amenorrhea (General/Secondary)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Any hormone panel abnormality in the context of absent periods warrants further evaluation'; Related Markers/Tests: LH, FSH, Prolactin, TSH, Testosterone

diseases.name: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated 17-OHP with clinical signs of androgen excess' - non-classic CAH is the principal differential for biochemical hyperandrogenism

diseases.name: Prediabetes
diseases.dm_basis: Possible Complications on the PCOS row name progression to impaired glucose tolerance and type 2 diabetes

cohorts.name: Adrenal Steroid Excess Pattern
cohorts.description: Raised 17-hydroxyprogesterone with androgen excess, the screening pattern for congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

evidence.citation: Speiser PW et al., Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia due to 21-Hydroxylase Deficiency, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2018;103:4043-88
evidence.note: Early morning 17-OHP as the first-line screening test, with ACTH stimulation for confirmation.

diseases.name: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated 17-OHP with clinical signs of androgen excess'; Related Markers/Tests: 17-hydroxyprogesterone, Testosterone; Severity/Urgency: 'emergency in salt-wasting neonatal crisis'

cohorts.name: Low Gonadotropin Pattern
cohorts.description: Low or inappropriately normal LH and FSH alongside low sex steroids - failure at the hypothalamic or pituitary level rather than the gonad.

supporting.label: Prolactin raised - can suppress the gonadotropin axis
TSH abnormal - thyroid dysfunction can disturb the cycle

evidence.citation: Gordon CM et al., Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Functional Hypothalamic Amenorrhea, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2017;102:1413-39
evidence.note: Low/normal gonadotropins with low estradiol in the setting of energy deficit, exercise or stress.

evidence.citation: Bhasin S et al., Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Testosterone Therapy in Men with Hypogonadism, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2018;103:1715-44
evidence.note: Low testosterone with low/normal LH and FSH defines secondary hypogonadism.

diseases.name: Functional Hypothalamic Amenorrhea
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low gonadotropins with low estrogen in the context of low body weight/excessive exercise/stress'; Related Markers/Tests: LH, FSH, Estradiol

diseases.name: Male Hypogonadism
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low testosterone with abnormal LH/FSH and symptomatic presentation'; Related Markers/Tests: Testosterone, LH, FSH, Semen Analysis parameters

diseases.name: Amenorrhea (General/Secondary)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Any hormone panel abnormality in the context of absent periods warrants further evaluation for the specific underlying cause'

diseases.name: Hyperprolactinemia
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Significantly elevated prolactin with compatible symptoms' - a treatable cause of gonadotropin suppression

cohorts.name: High Gonadotropin Pattern
cohorts.description: Raised LH and FSH with low sex steroids - the gonad is failing and the pituitary is compensating.

supporting.label: Sperm concentration low - primary testicular failure pattern

evidence.citation: Harlow SD et al., STRAW+10 Staging of Reproductive Aging, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2012;97:1159-68
evidence.note: Rising FSH with falling estradiol across the menopausal transition.

evidence.citation: Bhasin S et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2018;103:1715-44
evidence.note: Low testosterone with raised LH/FSH defines primary (testicular) hypogonadism.

diseases.name: Menopause/Perimenopause
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated FSH with low estradiol and 12+ months of absent periods (confirms menopause)'; Related Markers/Tests: FSH, Estradiol

diseases.name: Male Hypogonadism
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low testosterone with abnormal LH/FSH and symptomatic presentation'

diseases.name: Amenorrhea (General/Secondary)
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: LH, FSH, Prolactin, TSH, Testosterone as the initial hormonal workup panel

diseases.name: Precocious Puberty
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated LH/FSH with physical pubertal signs well before expected age' - applies only to paediatric patients, which this cohort cannot establish from lab data alone

cohorts.name: Raised Prolactin
cohorts.description: Prolactin above range, which suppresses the gonadotropin axis and is a common reversible cause of cycle disturbance and infertility.

supporting.label: TSH raised - primary hypothyroidism is a recognised cause of secondary hyperprolactinaemia

evidence.citation: Melmed S et al., Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Diagnosis and Treatment of Hyperprolactinemia, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2011;96:273-88
evidence.note: Confirmation on a repeat sample, exclusion of hypothyroidism, medication and macroprolactin before imaging.

diseases.name: Hyperprolactinemia
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Significantly elevated prolactin with compatible symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: Prolactin

diseases.name: Amenorrhea (General/Secondary)
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests lists Prolactin among the initial hormonal workup panel for absent periods

diseases.name: Hypothyroidism
diseases.dm_basis: Cross-linked because primary hypothyroidism can raise prolactin; the TSH result distinguishes the two

cohorts.name: Cortisol Excess Pattern
cohorts.description: Cortisol above range. Screening only - the clinical reference requires dynamic suppression testing to confirm.

supporting.label: ACTH abnormal - helps localise the source
Hypokalaemia - mineralocorticoid effect of cortisol excess
Glucose raised - steroid effect on glucose handling

evidence.citation: Nieman LK et al., Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: The Diagnosis of Cushing's Syndrome, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2008;93:1526-40
evidence.note: A single random cortisol is insufficient; 1 mg dexamethasone suppression, late-night salivary cortisol or 24-h urinary free cortisol are required.

diseases.name: Cushing's Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated cortisol not suppressed by dexamethasone testing, with classic physical features'; Related Markers/Tests: Cortisol (serum/salivary), ACTH. Weight held moderate because the indicator requires dynamic testing this cohort cannot perform.

cohorts.name: Adrenal Insufficiency Pattern
cohorts.description: Low sodium with raised potassium and a low cortisol - the electrolyte and hormone signature of mineralocorticoid and glucocorticoid deficiency.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The clinical reference Addison's Disease row itself spans Hormones and Electrolyte Profile and names 'Low sodium with high potassium and low cortisol' - a pattern that cannot be seen from either profile alone.

evidence.citation: Bornstein SR et al., Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Primary Adrenal Insufficiency, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2016;101:364-89
evidence.note: Hyponatraemia with hyperkalaemia and low morning cortisol; ACTH stimulation testing confirms.

diseases.name: Addison's Disease
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low sodium with high potassium and low cortisol'; Related Markers/Tests: Cortisol, Sodium, Potassium, ACTH; Severity/Urgency: 'emergency if adrenal crisis'

diseases.name: Sodium Imbalance (Hyponatremia/Hypernatremia)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Sodium persistently outside 136-145 mmol/L'

diseases.name: Potassium Imbalance (Hyperkalemia/Hypokalemia)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Potassium significantly outside the reference range'

cohorts.name: Growth Hormone Axis Excess
cohorts.description: Raised IGF-1, the integrated marker of growth hormone secretion.

triggers.label: Growth hormone above range (a single random level is of limited value)

supporting.label: Glucose raised - growth hormone antagonises insulin
Prolactin raised - co-secreting pituitary lesions occur

evidence.citation: Katznelson L et al., Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Acromegaly, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2014;99:3933-51
evidence.note: Age-normalised IGF-1 as the screening test; random GH is unreliable, oral glucose suppression confirms.

diseases.name: Acromegaly
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated IGF-1/GH with characteristic physical changes'; Related Markers/Tests: Growth Hormone, IGF-1

cohorts.name: Bone Mineral Deficiency Pattern
cohorts.description: Vitamin D deficiency with low or low-normal calcium and phosphate, with or without a compensatory rise in PTH - the pattern behind defective bone mineralisation.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: The clinical reference Osteomalacia/Rickets row spans Bone Health and Vitamin Profile and names Vitamin D, Calcium and Phosphorus together - drawing on the Vitamin Profile and Electrolyte Profile at once. Alkaline phosphatase from the Liver Profile is admitted as a bone-turnover marker.

supporting.label: PTH raised - secondary hyperparathyroidism compensating for low vitamin D
Alkaline phosphatase raised - increased bone turnover
Albumin low - total calcium under-reads true ionised calcium

evidence.citation: Holick MF et al., Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Evaluation, Treatment, and Prevention of Vitamin D Deficiency, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2011;96:1911-30
evidence.note: 25(OH)D thresholds: deficiency <20 ng/mL, insufficiency 21-29 ng/mL.

evidence.citation: Uday S, Hogler W, Calcif Tissue Int 2020;106:14-29
evidence.note: Biochemical staging of nutritional rickets/osteomalacia: raised ALP and PTH with low or low-normal calcium and phosphate.

diseases.name: Vitamin D Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Vitamin D level in the deficient range, especially with elevated PTH or low calcium'; Related Markers/Tests: Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy)

diseases.name: Osteomalacia/Rickets
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low Vitamin D with low or low-normal Calcium/Phosphorus, especially with bone pain'; Related Markers/Tests: Vitamin D, Calcium, Phosphorus

diseases.name: Osteoporosis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low bone-relevant markers (e.g. Vitamin D) in an at-risk individual'; Related Markers/Tests: Calcium, Vitamin D, Phosphorus

diseases.name: Hyperparathyroidism
diseases.dm_basis: Secondary hyperparathyroidism from vitamin D deficiency must be distinguished from the primary form, where calcium is high rather than low

diseases.name: Malabsorption Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests lists 'Vitamin D/B12/Folate' among the malabsorption marker set

cohorts.name: Raised Alkaline Phosphatase with Normal Calcium and Phosphate
cohorts.description: Alkaline phosphatase raised while calcium and phosphate stay normal - the biochemical signature of increased bone turnover rather than a mineral deficiency or a parathyroid problem.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: Alkaline phosphatase sits in the Liver Profile but is a bone turnover marker too. Reading it against Calcium and Phosphorus from the Electrolyte Profile is what separates a bone source from a hepatobiliary one.

supporting.label: Calcium normal - argues against hyperparathyroidism and malignancy
GGT normal - points to a bone rather than hepatobiliary source of the ALP
Vitamin D adequate - argues against osteomalacia as the cause

evidence.citation: Ralston SH et al., Diagnosis and Management of Paget's Disease of Bone in Adults, J Bone Miner Res 2019;34:579-604
evidence.note: Raised total alkaline phosphatase with normal calcium and phosphate is the characteristic biochemical picture; radionuclide bone scan and radiographs confirm.

evidence.citation: Singer FR et al., Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Paget's Disease of Bone, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2014;99:4408-22
evidence.note: ALP as the primary biochemical marker of disease activity, with a bone-specific isoenzyme or GGT used to exclude a hepatic source.

diseases.name: Paget's Disease of Bone
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Normal calcium/phosphorus but clinical suspicion (bone pain/deformity) in an older adult, particularly with an elevated alkaline phosphatase on other testing'; Related Markers/Tests: Calcium, Phosphorus

cohorts.name: Hypercalcaemia Pattern
cohorts.description: Raised calcium. The accompanying PTH and phosphate determine whether this is parathyroid-driven or something else.

supporting.label: PTH raised despite hypercalcaemia - inappropriate, suggests a parathyroid source
Phosphorus low - the classic accompaniment of parathyroid hormone excess
Calcium at or above 12 mg/dL - severe
Globulin raised - consider a paraproteinaemia instead
Total protein raised - together with hypercalcaemia this points toward a paraproteinaemia

evidence.citation: Bilezikian JP et al., Evaluation and Management of Primary Hyperparathyroidism: 2022 Workshop Guidelines, J Bone Miner Res 2022;37:2293-2314
evidence.note: Raised calcium with a non-suppressed PTH and low phosphate defines primary hyperparathyroidism.

evidence.citation: Rajkumar SV et al., Lancet Oncol 2014;15:e538-48
evidence.note: Hypercalcaemia as a CRAB feature of myeloma - the principal PTH-independent differential.

diseases.name: Hyperparathyroidism
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated calcium with elevated PTH, especially with low phosphorus'; Related Markers/Tests: Calcium, Phosphorus; Severity/Urgency: 'urgent if severe hypercalcemia'

diseases.name: Multiple Myeloma
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated total protein/globulin with hypercalcemia, anemia, or unexplained bone pain'

diseases.name: Paget's Disease of Bone
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators note calcium and phosphorus are 'usually normal' in Paget's, with ALP the abnormal marker

cohorts.name: Sodium Imbalance
cohorts.description: Sodium outside 136-145 mmol/L, the band named in the clinical reference. Rate of change matters as much as the absolute value.

supporting.label: Sodium below 125 mmol/L - severe, neurological risk
Sodium at or above 155 mmol/L - severe
Concentrated urine despite hyponatraemia - consistent with inappropriate ADH
TSH raised - hypothyroidism can cause hyponatraemia

evidence.citation: Spasovski G et al., Clinical Practice Guideline on Diagnosis and Treatment of Hyponatraemia, Eur J Endocrinol 2014;170:G1-47
evidence.note: Severity bands and the diagnostic algorithm including urine osmolality and volume status.

evidence.citation: Verbalis JG et al., Am J Med 2013;126(10 Suppl 1):S1-42
evidence.note: Diagnosis and management of hyponatraemia including SIADH criteria.

diseases.name: Sodium Imbalance (Hyponatremia/Hypernatremia)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Sodium persistently outside 136-145 mmol/L, especially with associated symptoms or rapid change'; Related Markers/Tests: Sodium (Na+)

diseases.name: SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Hyponatremia with concentrated urine (high urine osmolality) despite normal volume status'; Related Markers/Tests: Sodium (Na+)

diseases.name: Addison's Disease
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low sodium with high potassium and low cortisol'

diseases.name: Diabetes Insipidus
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Very low urine specific gravity with high serum sodium'

cohorts.name: Potassium Imbalance
cohorts.description: Potassium outside range. Significant because of the effect on cardiac conduction rather than symptoms.

supporting.label: Potassium at or above 6.0 mmol/L - risk of cardiac arrhythmia
Bicarbonate abnormal - acid-base shifts move potassium across cell membranes

evidence.citation: Palmer BF, Clegg DJ, N Engl J Med 2015;373:60-72
evidence.note: Hyperkalaemia: renal impairment and drug effects as leading causes; ECG changes drive urgency.

evidence.citation: Kardalas E et al., Endocr Connect 2018;7:R135-46
evidence.note: Hypokalaemia: causes, thresholds and cardiac consequences.

diseases.name: Potassium Imbalance (Hyperkalemia/Hypokalemia)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Potassium significantly outside the reference range, particularly with ECG changes or use of potassium-affecting medications'; Related Markers/Tests: Potassium (K+)

diseases.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
diseases.dm_basis: Impaired potassium excretion is a recognised feature of reduced filtration

diseases.name: Addison's Disease
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low sodium with high potassium and low cortisol'

cohorts.name: Acid-Base Disturbance
cohorts.description: Bicarbonate or pH outside range, with the anion gap used to separate the causes.

evidence.citation: Berend K, de Vries APJ, Gans ROB, N Engl J Med 2014;371:1434-45
evidence.note: Physiological approach to acid-base disorders using bicarbonate, pH and the anion gap.

evidence.citation: Kraut JA, Madias NE, Nat Rev Nephrol 2010;6:274-85
evidence.note: Metabolic acidosis: classification by anion gap and clinical context.

diseases.name: Metabolic Acidosis/Alkalosis
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Electrolyte pattern suggesting a wide anion gap or clinical context (vomiting, diarrhea, kidney disease, uncontrolled diabetes) consistent with acid-base disturbance'; Related Markers/Tests: Sodium, Potassium, Chloride (used to estimate anion gap)

diseases.name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'High glucose with positive urine ketones and low blood pH'

diseases.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
diseases.dm_basis: Metabolic acidosis is a recognised complication of advanced CKD

cohorts.name: Zinc Deficiency
cohorts.description: Zinc below range, most often from poor intake or malabsorption.

supporting.label: Albumin low - zinc is albumin-bound, and low albumin also suggests poor nutrition

evidence.citation: King JC et al., J Nutr 2016;146:858S-885S
evidence.note: Biomarkers of zinc status; serum zinc is the most practical though imperfect indicator.

diseases.name: Zinc Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Low zinc level with matching clinical signs, especially in malabsorption or poor dietary intake'; Related Markers/Tests: Zinc (urine)

diseases.name: Malabsorption Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Chronic diarrhea with steatorrhea plus multiple vitamin/mineral deficiencies'

cohorts.name: Multiple Micronutrient Deficiency Pattern
cohorts.description: Several unrelated micronutrients low at once, which points to impaired absorption rather than a single dietary gap.
cohorts.cross_profile_rationale: This cohort exists precisely because no single profile can identify malabsorption. The clinical reference row lists 'Stool analysis (fecal fat), Vitamin D/B12/Folate, Iron studies, Total Protein' - four different profiles in one marker set.

supporting.label: Anti-tTG IgA raised - coeliac disease as the cause

evidence.citation: Nikaki K, Gupte GL, Curr Opin Clin Nutr Metab Care 2016;19:309-14
evidence.note: Multiple simultaneous micronutrient deficiencies as a marker of intestinal malabsorption.

evidence.citation: Rubio-Tapia A et al., ACG Clinical Guidelines: Diagnosis and Management of Celiac Disease, Am J Gastroenterol 2023;118:59-76
evidence.note: tTG-IgA with total IgA as first-line coeliac serology in patients with malabsorptive features.

diseases.name: Malabsorption Syndrome
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Chronic diarrhea with steatorrhea plus multiple vitamin/mineral deficiencies or unexplained weight loss'; Related Markers/Tests: Stool analysis (fecal fat), Vitamin D/B12/Folate, Iron studies, Total Protein

diseases.name: Celiac Disease
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated tTG-IgA with compatible symptoms or unexplained iron/folate deficiency'

diseases.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Crohn's Disease/Ulcerative Colitis)
diseases.dm_basis: Possible Complications on the IBD row include malabsorption and nutritional deficiency

diseases.name: Vitamin B12 Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: Vitamin B12

diseases.name: Vitamin D Deficiency
diseases.dm_basis: Related Markers/Tests: Vitamin D (25-Hydroxy)

cohorts.name: Raised Heavy Metal Level
cohorts.description: One or more toxic metals above the reference value, which should prompt a search for the exposure source.

triggers.label: Blood lead at or above the CDC reference value of 3.5 ug/dL

supporting.label: Anaemia - lead interferes with haem synthesis
Creatinine raised - cadmium and mercury are nephrotoxic
Albuminuria - tubular injury marker in cadmium exposure

evidence.citation: CDC, Blood Lead Reference Value, 2021 (3.5 ug/dL)
evidence.note: Population-based reference value above which follow-up is recommended; there is no safe blood lead level.

evidence.citation: Satarug S et al., Environ Health Perspect 2010;118:182-90
evidence.note: Cadmium exposure and renal tubular dysfunction at low body burdens.

evidence.citation: Bernhoft RA, J Environ Public Health 2012;2012:460508
evidence.note: Mercury toxicity: neurological and renal manifestations.

diseases.name: Lead Poisoning
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated blood Lead level, especially in children or occupationally exposed adults'; Related Markers/Tests: Lead (blood)

diseases.name: Mercury Toxicity
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated Mercury level with neurological or renal symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: Mercury (blood)

diseases.name: Arsenic Poisoning
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated Arsenic level with consistent GI or skin symptoms'; Related Markers/Tests: Arsenic (blood)

diseases.name: Cadmium Toxicity
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated Cadmium level with signs of renal impairment'; Related Markers/Tests: Cadmium (blood/serum)

diseases.name: Chronic Heavy Metal Exposure (Aluminum/Cobalt/Thallium)
diseases.dm_basis: High-Risk Indicators: 'Elevated level on repeat testing with a plausible exposure source'; Related Markers/Tests: Aluminum, Cobalt, Thallium
